docs.title: Introduction
docs.text: LRP2 is a scalable, end-to-end long-read proteogenomics pipeline built in Nextflow. It identifies and validates protein isoforms by integrating PacBio long-read RNA-seq with mass spectrometry. Starting from full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) reads and/or raw MS files, LRP2 performs transcript discovery, ORF prediction, differential analysis, and mass spectrometry-based protein identification.

docs.title: Pipeline Overview
docs.text:
The LRP2 Nextflow pipeline consists of five subworkflows:

Subworkflow Description 1. PacBio Isocall Align FLNC reads and collapse to isoforms with PacBio Isocall 2. Transcriptome Classify transcripts with SQANTI3, filter artifacts, assign deterministic hash-based isoform IDs 3. Predicted proteome Predict ORFs with CPAT, classify proteins with SQANTI protein 4. Multi-sample analysis Differential expression and usage (edgeR, DRIMSeq), differential splicing (LR LeafCutter, preliminary implementation) 5. Proteomics Build custom reference database, convert raw MS files, search with FragPipe or MetaMorpheus, map peptides to isoforms

docs.title: Citing LRP2
docs.text:
If you use LRP2 in your work, please cite our preprint:

Schertzer MD, Lewandowski JT, et al. LRP2: A proteogenomics pipeline for long-read informed protein isoform analysis and discovery. Manuscript in preparation.

LRP2 builds on the original LRP framework:

Miller, R. M., Jordan, B. T., Mehlferber, M. M., et al. 2022. "Enhanced protein isoform characterization through long-read proteogenomics." Genome Biology 23(1): 69. doi: 10.1186/s13059-022-02624-y

See the full citation list for all tools used by the pipeline.

docs.title: Support and Customization
docs.text:
LRP2 supports a range of customization:

  • HPC environment: SLURM and LSF schedulers with configurable partition/queue and cluster options; Singularity, Docker, or Conda containers
  • Input flexibility: RNA-only, protein-only, or paired RNA + protein samples; DDA or DIA mass spec data
  • Reference genomes: GENCODE human and mouse across multiple versions
  • Proteomics: alternative search engines (FragPipe or MetaMorpheus) and customizable FragPipe workflows

We welcome input from the community. Please open an Issue if you have a use case not covered by the defaults.

docs.title: Issues and Bug Reports
docs.text:
For bug reports, feature requests, or general issues, please open an Issue: github.com/sheynkman-lab/LRP2/issues

When reporting an issue, please attach the following files to your Issue: 1. Your run logfile (.nextflow.log) 2. Your samplesheet.csv file for the run

Additionally, please share the following details in the body of your Issue:

  1. Your command line and configuration
  2. Nextflow version and executor (local, SLURM, LSF)
  3. A brief overview of your data (number of samples, read depth / file sizes, etc.)
  4. Your exact error message(s) and any other relevant log files (e.g. any other relevant logs for individual processes from the work/ directory)

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Nextflow ≥ 24.04.2 (installation guide)
  • Singularity/Apptainer or Docker for containerized dependencies

docs.title: Containers
docs.text:
LRP2 uses containers to manage software dependencies. Containers allow for the packaging of libraries, code, and configurations such that each tool in the pipeline can be reliably run in any computing environment without compatibility issues.

To run LRP2, you must have one of the following installed:

docs.title: 1. Singularity/Apptainer (required for HPC)
docs.text: Most HPC systems have Singularity or Apptainer pre-installed as a module. You can check this by running module avail singularity or module avail apptainer. If not available, contact your HPC administrator or see Apptainer installation guide.

docs.title: 2. Docker (may be used for local systems)
docs.text:
Installation guides: Docker Desktop (Mac/Windows) or Docker Engine (Linux)

Docker on HPC

Docker requires root/admin privileges, and is typically not permitted on shared HPC systems. We therefore strongly recommend the use of Singularity/Apptainer.

The pipeline will automatically pull and cache container images on first run. Note that Singularity images are cached in work/singularity/ by default.

docs.title: 3. Conda (not recommended)
docs.text:
While LRP2 technically supports Conda environments as a fallback, we strongly discourage using Conda due to significant reproducibility limitations.

If you are interested in learning more about best practices for computational reproducibility, please refer to this paper.

Why shouldn't I use Conda?

In short, containers provide superior reproducibility because they freeze the entire software stack including the operating system, tools, and all dependencies at a specific point in time. This ensures analyses run identically across different systems and over many years. Conda environments, by contrast, are resolved dynamically at runtime based on the package ecosystem at that moment. This means fresh Conda builds may pull newer versions of dependencies (including critical components like R or Python), which can cause results to differ when reruns are done months or years later.

For these reasons, please always use Singularity/Apptainer or Docker for analyses unless you have a specific technical constraint that prevents container usage.

docs.title: Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/sheynkman-lab/LRP2.git
cd LRP2

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: Once you have installed the prerequisites and cloned the repository, proceed to the Quick Start guide to run the test dataset.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
HPC Setup

The Quick Start uses SLURM on a UVA Rivanna-style HPC setup, which is what the pipeline has been most extensively tested with. LSF is also supported via the lsf profile. For other schedulers, see Support and customization.

Specifics vary by cluster — account flags (-A), partition names (-p), and module names (nextflow, apptainer) may differ on your system. Check with your HPC documentation or admin.

docs.title: Start a Persistent Session
docs.text:
Start a persistent terminal session so the pipeline keeps running if you lose your connection:

screen -S lrp2

Screen Usage

To detach from screen, press Ctrl+A then D. To reattach later: screen -r lrp2.

Certain HPC systems (e.g. UVA Rivanna) only support screen. On systems that support it, you can use the tmux terminal multiplexer instead by running tmux new -s lrp2.

docs.title: Request an Interactive Job
docs.text:
Request an interactive job with enough resources for the test dataset:

salloc -c 4 --mem=64G -p your_slurm_partition -A your_allocation --time=4:00:00

Adjust for Your System

Replace your_slurm_partition with your SLURM partition and your_allocation with your SLURM allocation group. UVA Rivanna users can substitute ijob for salloc. The -c (CPUs), --mem (memory), and --time values above are sufficient for the test dataset, but should be increased for larger datasets.

docs.title: Load Required Modules
docs.text: module load nextflow apptainer

docs.title: Run the RNA-only Test Dataset
docs.text:
From the LRP2 directory:

nextflow run . \
    -profile test_rna,singularity,slurm \
    --outdir test_rna_results \
    --hpc_queue your_queue

Configuration Notes

  • Replace your_queue with your cluster's partition (SLURM) or queue (LSF) name.
  • If your cluster requires additional scheduler options such as account strings or QOS flags, pass them via --hpc_cluster_options (e.g., --hpc_cluster_options '-A your_allocation' for SLURM, --hpc_cluster_options '-P your_project' for LSF).
  • LSF users: swap slurm for lsf in the profile.
  • See HPC Scheduler Options for more details.

Running Locally

To run locally on your current node instead of submitting to SLURM, drop the slurm profile: -profile test_rna,singularity.

docs.title: Run the RNA + DDA Proteomics Test Dataset
Step 1: Get a FragPipe Academic License Token
docs.text:
FragPipe requires an academic license for MSFragger, IonQuant, and diaTracer. Before using FragPipe in LRP2 for the first time, review the academic license agreement. To accept the license and request a one-time token, run the following curl command in your terminal, substituting your information for YOUR_FIRST_NAME, YOUR_LAST_NAME, YOUR_EMAIL, and YOUR_INSTITUTION:

curl --location --request POST \
    'https://msfragger-upgrader.nesvilab.org/upgrader/upgrade_download.php' \
    --form 'transfer="academic"' \
    --form 'agreement2="true"' \
    --form 'agreement3="true"' \
    --form "first_name=YOUR_FIRST_NAME" \
    --form "last_name=YOUR_LAST_NAME" \
    --form "email=YOUR_EMAIL" \
    --form "organization=YOUR_INSTITUTION" \
    --form "download=4.4.1\$zip" \
    --form 'is_fragpipe="true"' \
    > /dev/null 2>&1

Token Expiration

Tokens expire quickly. You will need a new token for each run.

Non-Academic Users

See Support and customization for alternative options.

docs.title: Step 2: Check Your Email
docs.text: Check your email for a 6-digit token.

docs.title: Step 3: Run the Test
docs.text:
From the LRP2 directory:

nextflow run . \
    -profile test_dda,singularity,slurm \
    --outdir test_results_dda \
    --fragpipe_token "YOUR_TOKEN" \
    --hpc_queue your_queue

Note

The test_dda profile automatically sets --protein_search fragpipe and --fragpipe_license_accept true, which are arguments you need to specify when you want to run FragPipe on your own data.

Running Locally

To run locally instead of submitting to SLURM, drop the slurm profile: -profile test_dda,singularity.

docs.text:
After successfully running the test dataset, you are now ready to run the pipeline on your data! Please refer to the following documentation:

docs.title: System Requirements and HPC Recommendations
docs.text: LRP2 is primarily designed for High-Performance Computing (HPC) environments. Although the test dataset can run on a local machine (minimum of 4 CPUs and 32GB RAM recommended), real-world datasets require substantial computational resources to be processed efficiently.

docs.title: Minimum Requirements for Test Dataset
docs.text:
• CPUs: 4 cores
  • Memory: 32 GB RAM
  • Storage: At least 50 GB free space for test data and intermediate files

docs.title: HPC Recommendations
docs.text:
For production runs with real-world datasets:

  • Scheduler: SLURM or LSF
  • Container runtime: Singularity/Apptainer
  • Persistent session: screen or tmux for long-running jobs

docs.title: Resource Allocation
docs.text:
Resource allocation works on two levels:

  1. The driver job: Modest resources are sufficient for the driver script, as these are used by Nextflow for task submission and pipeline orchestration. Typically 1 CPU and 40GB memory is adequate.

  2. Individual pipeline tasks: CPUs, memory, and time per process are handled automatically by LRP2's internal configuration. You do not need to specify these on the command line. To customize, edit conf/base.config directly to set values for a process label (process_low, process_medium, process_high, etc.)

docs.title: Software Requirements
docs.text:
• Nextflow ≥ 24.04.2
  • Singularity/Apptainer or Docker
  • Standard Unix utilities (bash, git, curl)

docs.title: Network Requirements
docs.text: The pipeline will download reference genomes (assuming you are using an inbuilt GENCODE reference with the --genome parameter) and container images on first run. Please ensure that your system has internet access, or that you have pre-staged these resources prior to running.

docs.title: Output Files
docs.text: This page provides detailed information about the output files generated by each subworkflow.

docs.title: File Naming Conventions
docs.text:
Most output files follow the naming pattern [dataset_name].[subworkflow].[module].[file_type].

For S4 Multisample Analysis outputs, the prefix is the condition comparison name (e.g. control_vs_treatment).

For proteomics outputs, each distinct proteomics search run has results stored in its own distinct subdirectory in ${resultsDir}/S5_PROTEOMICS/M3_FRAGPIPE/ according to its sample name in the samplesheet.

docs.title: M5_ISOCALL_CALL
docs.text:
• *.isocall.isoforms.gtf.gz: GTF/GFF format transcript structures
  • *.isocall.count_matrix.csv: Transcript count matrix showing read counts per isoform

docs.title: M1_SQANTI_QC
docs.text:
• *.transcriptome.SQANTI_classification.txt: Comprehensive transcript classification with structural categories (FSM, ISM, NIC, NNC, etc.), splice junction information, and quality metrics
  • *.transcriptome.gtf: SQANTI-annotated transcript structures in GTF format
  • *.transcriptome.fasta: SQANTI-annotated transcript sequences in FASTA format
  • *.transcriptome.junctions.txt: Splice junction catalog with genomic coordinates and support

docs.title: M2_GENERATE_HASHIDS
docs.text:
• *.transcriptome.hashids_mapping.txt: Maps transcript IDs to unique hash identifiers for reproducible naming across samples and analyses
  • *.transcriptome.psl: PSL format alignment file

docs.title: M3_FILTER_TRANSCRIPTOME
docs.text:
• *.transcriptome.filtered.gtf: Filtered transcriptome in GTF format (technical artifacts removed)
  • *.transcriptome.filtered.bed: Filtered transcriptome in BED12 format
  • *.transcriptome.filtered.fasta: Filtered transcript sequences
  • *.transcriptome.filtered_hashids_with_cpm.txt: Count matrix with CPM normalization for filtered transcripts
  • *.transcriptome.all_hashids_with_cpm.txt: Count matrix with CPM for all transcripts (pre-filtering)
  • *.transcriptome.filtered_SQANTI_classification.txt: SQANTI classification file for filtered transcripts only

docs.title: M1_CPAT_ORF
docs.text:
• *.predicted_proteome.CPAT.ORF_prob.tsv: All predicted ORFs with coding probability scores
  • *.predicted_proteome.CPAT.ORF_prob.best.tsv: Single best ORF per transcript based on coding potential
  • *.predicted_proteome.CPAT.ORF_seqs.fa: ORF sequences in FASTA format
  • *.predicted_proteome.CPAT.no_ORF.txt: Transcripts with no ORF identified
  • *.predicted_proteome.CPAT.error: Error log from CPAT

docs.title: M2_FILTER_CPAT
docs.text:
• *.predicted_proteome.best_ORF.gtf: GTF with exon and CDS annotations for the single best ORF per transcript
  • *.predicted_proteome.CPAT_ORFs_mapped.tsv: Detailed mapping of all ORFs to transcripts

This module selects the single most likely ORF per transcript based on CPAT scores, start codon presence, and ORF length.

docs.title: M3_SQANTI_PROTEIN
docs.text: • *.predicted_proteome.best_ORF_SQANTI_classification.tsv: Protein isoform classification including ORF completeness, protein structural categories, and comparison to reference proteins

docs.title: M4_PROTEIN_CLASSIFICATION
docs.text:
• *.predicted_proteome.best_ORF_summary.txt: Summary statistics for ORF predictions
  • *.predicted_proteome.best_ORF.fa: Protein sequences for all best ORFs in FASTA format
  • *.predicted_proteome.collapsed_high_confidence_ORF.gtf: GTF with protein-coding transcripts collapsed to distinct ORFs
  • *.predicted_proteome.collapsed_high_confidence_ORF.bed: BED12 format of high-confidence ORFs
  • *.predicted_proteome.collapsed_high_confidence_ORF_hashids_with_cpm.txt: Count matrix with CPM normalization for distinct ORFs

docs.title: M1_LEAFCUTTER_LONGREAD
docs.text:
• *.lr_leafcutter.ds_cluster_significance.txt: Statistical significance of differential splicing at the cluster level (q-values, p-values)
  • *.lr_leafcutter.ds_effect_sizes.txt: Effect sizes showing magnitude and direction of intron usage changes between conditions
  • *.lr_leafcutter.subisoform_clusters.txt: Intron clusters defining groups of alternatively spliced introns
  • *.lr_leafcutter.perind_numers.counts.gz: Counts matrix showing intron usage per individual sample
  • *.lr_leafcutter.groups_file.txt: Sample-to-condition mapping for differential analysis
  • lr_leafcutter.Rplots.pdf: Visualization plots (optional)

LeafCutter-LongRead identifies differential alternative splicing by quantifying intron excision ratios across samples, clustering introns by shared splice sites, and testing for differential usage between conditions.

docs.title: M2_DIFFERENTIAL_EXPRESSION
docs.text:
Differential Gene Expression (DGE):

  • *_DGE_edgeR_results.txt: Gene-level differential expression results (log2FC, FDR, p-values)
  • *_DGE_edgeR_raw_CPM_matrix.txt: Raw counts-per-million matrix
  • *_DGE_edgeR_normalized_CPM_matrix.txt: Normalized CPM matrix (library size corrected)
  • *_DGE_MD_plot.pdf: Mean-difference (MA) plot showing log2FC vs average expression

Differential Transcript Expression (DTE):

  • *_DTE_edgeR_results.txt: Transcript-level differential expression
  • *_DTE_edgeR_raw_CPM_matrix.txt: Raw CPM matrix for transcripts
  • *_DTE_edgeR_normalized_CPM_matrix.txt: Normalized CPM matrix for transcripts
  • *_DTE_MD_plot.pdf: Mean-difference plot for transcripts

Differential ORF Expression (DE_ORF):

  • *_DE_ORF_edgeR_results.txt: ORF-level differential expression
  • *_DE_ORF_edgeR_raw_CPM_matrix.txt: Raw CPM matrix for ORFs
  • *_DE_ORF_edgeR_normalized_CPM_matrix.txt: Normalized CPM matrix for ORFs
  • *_DE_ORF_MD_plot.pdf: Mean-difference plot for ORFs

Differential Transcript Usage (DTU):

  • *_DTU_transcript_DRIMSeq_summary.txt: Transcript usage differences within genes

Differential ORF Usage (DU_ORF):

  • *_DU_ORF_DRIMSeq_summary.txt: ORF usage differences within genes

docs.title: M1_BUILD_PROTEOME_REFERENCE
docs.text:
• *.proteomics.reference.fasta: Combined FASTA database for mass spectrometry searches (includes GENCODE reference proteins and, if run with RNA samples, LRP2-predicted proteins)
  • *.proteomics.reference.tsv: Metadata table mapping protein IDs to source (GENCODE/LRP2), gene names, isoform IDs, and classification

docs.title: M2_MSCONVERT_MZML
docs.text: • *.mzML: Mass spectrometry data in standard mzML format, converted from vendor-specific raw formats (e.g. .raw)

docs.title: M3_FRAGPIPE
docs.text:
• peptide.tsv: Peptide-level identifications with scores and quantification
  • combined_peptide.tsv: Combined peptide results across runs
  • protein.tsv: Protein-level identifications and quantification
  • psm.tsv: Peptide-spectrum matches (PSMs) with detailed scoring
  • Additional quantification and quality control files

docs.title: M4_NOVEL_PEPTIDES
docs.text:
• *.peptides.bed: Peptides mapped to genomic coordinates in BED12 format
  • *_peptide_summary.txt: Summary table classifying peptides as annotated or novel.

docs.title: pipeline_info/
docs.text:
• execution_report.html: Comprehensive report including resource usage per task (CPU, memory, time), task completion statistics, and failed tasks with error messages (if any)

  • execution_timeline.html: Interactive timeline visualization showing task start and end times, parallel execution patterns, and resource utilization over time

  • lrp2_software_versions.yml: Complete list of software versions used in the pipeline run for full reproducibility

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: For information about the directory structure and organization of these files, see Output Structure.

docs.title: Pipeline Output Structure
docs.text: Each subworkflow outputs to numbered module directories. The final module in each subworkflow typically contains the key results, while earlier modules contain intermediate files.

docs.title: Directory Structure
docs.text:
<outdir>/
├── S1_PACBIO_ISOCALL/
│   ├── M1_ISOCALL_ALIGN/
│   ├── M2_ISOCALL_PROFILE/
│   ├── M3_ISOCALL_PREP/
│   ├── M4_ISOCALL_MERGE/
│   └── M5_ISOCALL_CALL/                 # GTF of transcript structures and count matrix
├── S2_TRANSCRIPTOME/
│   ├── M1_SQANTI_QC/
│   ├── M2_GENERATE_HASHIDS/
│   └── M3_FILTER_TRANSCRIPTOME/         # GTF, BED12, DNA FASTA, count matrix of the refined transcriptome (technical artifacts removed)
├── S3_PREDICTED_PROTEOME/
│   ├── M1_CPAT_ORF/
│   ├── M2_FILTER_CPAT/                  # GTF with exon and CDS type columns for single best ORF identified per transcript
│   ├── M3_SQANTI_PROTEIN/
│   └── M4_PROTEIN_CLASSIFICATION/       # GTF, BED12, protein FASTA, count matrix collapsed to distinct ORFs
├── S4_MULTISAMPLE_ANALYSIS/             # (optional)
│   ├── M1_LEAFCUTTER_LONGREAD/          # Differential splicing results
│   └── M2_DIFFERENTIAL_EXPRESSION/      # Differential expression/usage
│       ├── differential_gene_expression/
│       │   ├── *_DGE_edgeR_results.txt
│       │   ├── *_DGE_edgeR_raw_CPM_matrix.txt
│       │   ├── *_DGE_edgeR_normalized_CPM_matrix.txt
│       │   └── *_DGE_MD_plot.pdf
│       ├── differential_transcript_expression/
│       │   ├── *_DTE_edgeR_results.txt
│       │   └── *_DTE_MD_plot.pdf
│       ├── differential_ORF_expression/
│       │   ├── *_DE_ORF_edgeR_results.txt
│       │   └── *_DE_ORF_MD_plot.pdf
│       ├── differential_transcript_usage/
│       │   └── *_DTU_transcript_DRIMSeq_summary.txt
│       └── differential_ORF_usage/
│           └── *_DU_ORF_DRIMSeq_summary.txt
├── S5_PROTEOMICS/                       # (optional)
│   ├── M1_BUILD_PROTEOME_REFERENCE/
│   ├── M2_MSCONVERT_MZML/
│   ├── M3_FRAGPIPE/
│   └── M4_NOVEL_PEPTIDES/               # BED12 of peptides mapped to genome, summary table of novel and annotated peptides mapped to isoforms
└── pipeline_info/                       # Execution reports and logs
    ├── execution_report.html
    ├── execution_timeline.html
    └── lrp2_software_versions.yml

docs.title: S1: PacBio Isocall
docs.text:
Location: S1_PACBIO_ISOCALL/M5_ISOCALL_CALL/

  • GTF of transcript structures
  • Count matrix

docs.title: S2: Transcriptome
docs.text:
Location: S2_TRANSCRIPTOME/M3_FILTER_TRANSCRIPTOME/

  • GTF, BED12, DNA FASTA
  • Count matrix of the refined transcriptome (technical artifacts removed)

docs.title: S3: Predicted Proteome
docs.text:
Intermediate: S3_PREDICTED_PROTEOME/M2_FILTER_CPAT/ - GTF with exon and CDS type columns for single best ORF identified per transcript

Final: S3_PREDICTED_PROTEOME/M4_PROTEIN_CLASSIFICATION/ - GTF, BED12, protein FASTA - Count matrix collapsed to distinct ORFs

docs.title: S4: Multisample Analysis (Optional)
docs.text:
Location: S4_MULTISAMPLE_ANALYSIS/

Includes differential expression/usage results: - Gene expression (DGE) - Transcript expression (DTE) - ORF expression (DE_ORF) - Transcript usage (DTU) - ORF usage (DU_ORF) - Differential splicing (LeafCutter)

docs.title: S5: Proteomics (Optional)
docs.text:
Location: S5_PROTEOMICS/M4_NOVEL_PEPTIDES/

  • BED12 of peptides mapped to genome
  • Summary table of novel and annotated peptides mapped to isoforms

docs.title: Pipeline Reports
docs.text:
Location: pipeline_info/

  • execution_report.html: Resource usage and task statistics
  • execution_timeline.html: Timeline visualization of task execution
  • lrp2_software_versions.yml: Versions of all software used

For detailed information about specific output files, see Output Files.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text: The pipeline automatically downloads the appropriate FASTA and GTF files based on your --genome selection. Species is auto-detected from --genome and determines which CPAT model (human or mouse) is used for ORF prediction.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: See conf/gencode_references.config for the full list of supported versions and their download URLs.

docs.title: Usage

--genome GRCh38.p14.v49

Custom Genomes

docs.title: Usage Overview
docs.text: This section provides detailed instructions for running the LRP2 pipeline on your own data.

docs.title: Before You Start
docs.text: Make sure you have completed the installation and successfully run the quick start test dataset.

docs.title: Running the Pipeline
docs.text: There are two main approaches to running LRP2:

docs.title: 1. Interactive Job (Test Data Only)
docs.text: Suitable for small test datasets. See the Quick Start guide.

docs.title: 2. Driver Shell Script (Recommended for Production)
docs.text:
For most datasets, we recommend running the pipeline from a driver shell script submitted to SLURM/LSF. This is more robust than running interactively since large datasets may exceed interactive job time limits or resource quotas.

See Running the Pipeline for detailed instructions.

docs.title: Key Topics
docs.text:
• Preparing Input Data: Format your samplesheet and prepare FLNC reads and mass spec files
  • Running the Pipeline: Execute LRP2 with production data
  • Profile Options: Choose container and executor profiles
  • Parameters: Complete reference for all pipeline parameters

docs.title: Getting Help
docs.text:
If you encounter issues:

  1. Check the parameters documentation to ensure correct configuration
  2. Review the output structure to verify results
  3. See the support page for how to get help

docs.title: Advanced Usage
docs.text: This page covers advanced usage modes that allow you to re-run specific subworkflows of the LRP2 pipeline independently, using outputs from previous runs. These modes are useful for iterative analyses and parameter optimization.

docs.title: Re-running S4 Multisample Analysis Only
docs.text:
If you have already completed a full LRP2 run and want to re-run just the differential analysis modules (S4 MULTISAMPLE ANALYSIS) with different parameters, you can use multisample-only mode by passing a samplesheet through --multisample_metadata, as well as paths to three required input transcript and ORF-level output files from a previous run.

This allows you to skip subworkflows S1-S3 (PacBio Isocall, Transcriptome, Predicted Proteome) and rerun only S4 (Multisample Analysis), which is useful for testing different statistical thresholds, filtering parameters, and/or condition subgroupings of your samples.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
nextflow run /path/to/LRP2 \
    --multisample_metadata samplesheet.csv \
    --transcripts_gtf results/S2_TRANSCRIPTOME/M3_FILTER_TRANSCRIPTOME/merged.transcriptome.filtered.gtf \
    --transcript_counts results/S2_TRANSCRIPTOME/M3_FILTER_TRANSCRIPTOME/merged.transcriptome.filtered_hashids_with_cpm.txt \
    --orf_counts results/S3_PREDICTED_PROTEOME/M4_PROTEIN_CLASSIFICATION/merged.predicted_proteome.collapsed_high_confidence_ORF_hashids_with_cpm.txt \
    --outdir results_reanalysis \
    --min_samples_per_intron 1 \
    --min_usage_ratio 0.05 \
    -profile singularity,slurm

docs.title: Required Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description --multisample_metadata Path to samplesheet CSV. Must have columns: sample_name, sample_path, condition or group, and sample_type. --transcripts_gtf Path to filtered transcriptome GTF from a previous run --transcript_counts Path to transcript counts file from a previous run --orf_counts Path to ORF counts file from a previous run --outdir Output directory for the reanalysis

docs.title: Metadata CSV Format
docs.text:
The metadata CSV passed to --multisample_metadata must have columns named sample_name, sample_path, condition or group, and sample_type.

Reusing Samplesheets

The standard samplesheet format will work for --multisample_metadata. However, if you are rerunning this for the same data with only different condition group labels for samples or minor parameter value changes, we recommend creating a unique samplesheet for each one and choosing a corresponding name for your output results directory to help keep your results organized and straightforward to differentiate between.

docs.title: Re-running S5 Proteomics Only
docs.text: If you have already generated a transcriptome and predicted proteome, you can run just the proteomics subworkflow (S5) by providing a samplesheet containing only protein samples along with the reference files from your previous run.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
nextflow run /path/to/LRP2 \
    --input samplesheet.csv \
    --outdir results \
    --genome GRCh38.p14.v49 \
    --S5_custom_protein_fasta S3_PREDICTED_PROTEOME/M4_PROTEIN_CLASSIFICATION/lrp2.predicted_proteome.best_ORF.fa \
    --S5_custom_cds_gtf S3_PREDICTED_PROTEOME/M2_FILTER_CPAT/lrp2.predicted_proteome.best_ORF.gtf \
    --S5_custom_counts S2_TRANSCRIPTOME/M3_FILTER_TRANSCRIPTOME/lrp2.transcriptome.all_hashids_with_cpm.txt \
    --protein_search fragpipe \
    --fragpipe_token "YOUR_TOKEN" \
    -profile singularity,slurm
--S5_custom_counts is optional. The count matrix must have transcript IDs matching --S5_custom_protein_fasta in the first column, and a CPM column whose name contains the sample_name used for your protein samples in the samplesheet.

These parameters apply only to proteomics-only runs. On a full pipeline run, the equivalent files are generated by S2 and S3 and used automatically.

docs.title: Required Parameters
docs.text: Parameter Description --S5_custom_protein_fasta Path to LRP2 protein FASTA from a previous S3 run --S5_custom_cds_gtf Path to LRP2 CDS GTF from a previous S3 run

docs.title: Optional Parameters
docs.text:
Parameter Description --S5_custom_counts Path to count matrix with matching transcript IDs and CPM columns with sample names

Warning

For proteomics-only mode to work correctly, your samplesheet should only contain sample_type=protein entries. Do not include any RNA samples. The pipeline will automatically detect the absence of RNA samples and skip S1-S4.

docs.title: Important Considerations
docs.text: If using an LRP2 protein FASTA from S3 containing ALL predicted ORFs, keep in mind that proteomic search spaces will be larger, which affects false discovery rates. For more targeted proteomics searches, you may want to pre-filter the LRP2 FASTA.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text: For a list of all available parameters and their descriptions, see the Parameters documentation.

docs.title: Input File Requirements
docs.text:
RNA samples must be provided as PacBio full-length non-chimeric (FLNC) reads as outputted by PacBio Isoseq refine, in either BAM or FASTQ format. It is assumed that input files are post-processed and have already undergone deconcatenation, demultiplexing, and primer removal. Do NOT provide raw subreads or CCS reads directly from the sequencer.

Protein samples may be either DDA or DIA, and can be provided in .mzML format or vendor-specific raw formats.

docs.title: Samplesheet Structure
docs.text: Prepare a comma-delimited samplesheet (.csv) describing your input data:

docs.title: Samplesheet Columns
docs.text: Column Description sample_name Each RNA sample must have a distinct value. Do not include any spaces in this value. sample_path Absolute path to the input file.• RNA samples should be PacBio FLNC .bam or .fastq files• Protein samples should be .raw or .mzML files condition Sample group (e.g., "control", "treatment"). Used for differential analysis, which performs pairwise comparisons between groups. Two or more groups are supported. If you do not want differential analysis, assign the same condition to all samples. Do not include any spaces in this value. sample_type Must be either RNA or protein. mass_spec_type Must be either DDA or DIA. Required for protein samples. For RNA samples, specify none for this column.

docs.title: Sample Naming Conventions
docs.text:
Naming Rules

RNA samples: Each RNA sample must have a unique sample_name. These are used by Isocall to label count matrix columns.

Protein samples: All raw files from the same biological sample (e.g., multiple fractions or injection replicates) must share the same sample_name so they are combined and searched together in FragPipe.

Matched RNA + protein samples: Use the same sample_name for the RNA and protein entries. The predicted proteome from that sample will be included in the proteomics search database.

Unmatched protein samples: If a protein sample has no matched RNA sample, assign it a sample_name that does not match any RNA sample. In this case, only the GENCODE reference proteome will be used as the proteomics search database.

docs.title: Example Samplesheet
docs.text:
sample_name,sample_path,condition,sample_type,mass_spec_type
K562_rep1,/path/to/K562_rep1.bam,K562,RNA,none
K562_rep2,/path/to/K562_rep2.bam,K562,RNA,none
HepG2_rep1,/path/to/HepG2_rep1.bam,HepG2,RNA,none
HepG2_rep2,/path/to/HepG2_rep2.bam,HepG2,RNA,none
K562_rep1,/path/to/K562_rep1_F1.raw,K562,protein,DDA
K562_rep1,/path/to/K562_rep1_F2.raw,K562,protein,DDA
HepG2_rep1,/path/to/HepG2_rep1.raw,HepG2,protein,DDA

In this example:

  • Two RNA samples per condition (K562 and HepG2)
  • K562 protein sample has 2 fractions that will be searched together
  • HepG2 protein sample has 1 file
  • RNA and protein samples are matched by sample_name

docs.title: Parameters
docs.text:
For a complete list of parameters:

nextflow run /path/to/LRP2 --help

Parameter Configuration

Please provide pipeline parameters via the CLI as shown or using the Nextflow -params-file option. Custom config files including those provided by the -c Nextflow option can be used to provide any configuration other than parameters.

docs.title: Input/Output
docs.text: Parameter Description Default --input Path to samplesheet CSV (required) — --outdir Path to output directory (required) — --dataset_name Run identifier used for output prefixes merged --genome Reference genome version GRCh38.p14.v49

docs.title: HPC Scheduler Options
docs.text: Parameter Description Default --hpc_queue SLURM/LSF partition/queue name — --hpc_cluster_options Additional scheduler-specific options (e.g., '-A my_alloc' for SLURM, '-P my_project' for LSF) —

docs.title: Example Usage
docs.text:
SLURM with account requirement:

--hpc_queue standard --hpc_cluster_options '-A my_allocation'

LSF with project requirement:

--hpc_queue normal --hpc_cluster_options '-P my_project'

docs.title: S1 PacBio Isocall
docs.text: Parameter Description Default --min_read_support Minimum read support for transcripts 3 --isocall_config Path to custom Isocall configuration TOML file bin/isocall_config.toml

docs.title: S2 Transcriptome
docs.text: Parameter Description Default --protein_coding_filter Keep only protein-coding genes true --internal_priming_filter Remove internal priming artifacts true --template_switching_filter Remove template switching artifacts true --transcript_class_keep Structural categories to retain (FSM, ISM, NIC, NNC, ALL) FSM,ISM,NIC,NNC

docs.title: S3 Predicted Proteome
docs.text: Parameter Description Default --min_orf Minimum ORF length in nucleotides 75 --cpat_coding_threshold Coding probability threshold 0.364 (human), 0.44 (mouse) --protein_class_keep Protein categories to retain FPM,NPC,NPE

docs.title: S4 Multisample Analysis
docs.text: Parameter Description Default --min_samples_per_intron Minimum samples per intron for leafcutter 2 --min_samples_per_group Minimum samples per group for leafcutter 1 --min_usage_ratio Minimum junction usage ratio for filtering 0.01

docs.title: S5 Proteomics
docs.text: Parameter Description Default --protein_search Search engine: fragpipe (required) - --fragpipe_token Single-use academic license token for FragPipe (required if --protein_search fragpipe). See Quick Start for how to obtain one. — --fragpipe_workflow Path to a custom FragPipe workflow file specifying search parameters (modifications, enzymes, etc.) default is selected by mass_spec_type

docs.title: Profile Options
docs.text: Nextflow profiles control how the pipeline executes. Multiple profiles can be combined using commas (e.g., -profile test_rna,singularity,slurm).

docs.title: Container Profiles (choose ONE)
docs.text:
Profile Description Best For singularity Use Singularity/Apptainer containers HPC systems (most common) docker Use Docker containers Local machines with Docker installed conda Use Conda environments Systems without container support (slower)

Conda Not Recommended

We have extensively tested the pipeline with singularity locally and on HPC systems, and recommend its usage. You may use docker on local machines. We do not recommend the use of conda except as a last resort due to it lacking the same reproducibility as containers.

docs.title: Executor Profiles (recommended)
docs.text:
Profile Description When to Use slurm Submit jobs to SLURM scheduler on an HPC HPC environment with SLURM lsf Submit jobs to LSF scheduler on an HPC HPC environment with LSF

Local Execution

When using slurm or lsf, Nextflow submits individual pipeline tasks as separate jobs. Without a scheduler profile, all tasks run on the node where you launch Nextflow (requires sufficient resources). If you intend to run locally, you may need to lower resource requirements in conf/base.config.

docs.title: Test Profiles
docs.text: Profile Description Dataset test_rna RNA-only test dataset Runs RNA subworkflows (S1 - S4) test_dda RNA + DDA proteomics test Runs all subworkflows (S1 - S5) with FragPipe DDA search

docs.title: HPC with SLURM (recommended for production)
docs.text: -profile singularity,slurm

docs.title: Quick RNA test on HPC
docs.text: -profile test_rna,singularity,slurm

docs.title: Local machine with Docker
docs.text: -profile docker

docs.title: Running the Pipeline
docs.text: For most datasets, we recommend running the pipeline from a driver shell script submitted to SLURM/LSF. This is more robust than running interactively (as shown in the Quick Start for test data), since large datasets may exceed interactive job time limits or resource quotas.

docs.title: SLURM Example
docs.text:
Create a run_lrp2.sh script with your SLURM run parameters:

#!/bin/bash

#SBATCH --job-name=lrp2_driver
#SBATCH --partition=your_partition
#SBATCH --account=your_allocation
#SBATCH --time=72:00:00
#SBATCH --cpus-per-task=1
#SBATCH --mem=40G

module load nextflow apptainer

nextflow run /path/to/LRP2 \
    --input samplesheet.csv \
    --outdir results \
    --dataset_name my_dataset \
    --genome GRCh38.p14.v49 \
    --protein_search fragpipe \
    --fragpipe_token "YOUR_TOKEN" \
    --hpc_queue your_queue \
    -profile singularity,slurm

Submit with:

sbatch run_lrp2.sh

docs.title: LSF Example
docs.text:
For LSF systems, use #BSUB directives instead:

#!/bin/bash

#BSUB -J lrp2_driver
#BSUB -q your_queue
#BSUB -P your_project
#BSUB -W 72:00
#BSUB -n 1
#BSUB -M 40G

module load nextflow apptainer

nextflow run /path/to/LRP2 \
    --input samplesheet.csv \
    --outdir results \
    --dataset_name my_dataset \
    --genome GRCh38.p14.v49 \
    --protein_search fragpipe \
    --fragpipe_token "YOUR_TOKEN" \
    --hpc_queue your_queue \
    --hpc_cluster_options '-P your_project' \
    -profile singularity,lsf

Submit with:

bsub < run_lrp2.sh

docs.title: Important Notes
docs.text:
Resource Allocation

Resource allocation works on two levels:

  1. The driver job (#SBATCH or #BSUB directives in the shell script): modest resources are sufficient — Nextflow itself only orchestrates submissions and doesn't run the heavy work.

  2. Individual pipeline tasks (CPUs, memory, time per process): handled automatically by LRP2's internal configuration. You do not need to specify these on the command line. To customize, edit conf/base.config.

FragPipe Token

Include --fragpipe_token only if running the proteomics subworkflow. See Quick Start for obtaining a token.

Differential Analysis

Differential analysis runs automatically when two or more conditions are present in the samplesheet.

docs.title: Customization
docs.text:
Customize the above template for your HPC:

  • SLURM/LSF directives: partition/queue, account/project
  • Module names: nextflow, apptainer (may be singularity on some systems)
  • Pipeline parameters: --hpc_queue and --hpc_cluster_options

For other schedulers, see the Support page.
